content: Megestrol tablets are prescribed to alleviate symptoms and reduce suffering in patients with advanced breast cancer and advanced endometrial cancer, which originates in the uterine lining. The liquid suspension form of megestrol is used to address loss of appetite, malnutrition, and severe weight loss in individuals with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). However, it should not be used to prevent appetite loss or weight loss in patients who have not yet developed these conditions. Megestrol is a synthetic version of the hormone progesterone. It works by influencing female hormones that contribute to cancer growth and promotes weight gain by stimulating appetite. Megestrol is available in tablet form, as a liquid suspension, and as a concentrated suspension (Megace ES), all of which are taken orally. Tablets and the regular suspension are typically taken multiple times daily, while the concentrated suspension is usually taken once daily. It is important to take megestrol at the same time(s) each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. The concentrated suspension has a different dosage than the regular suspension, so do not switch between the two without consulting your doctor. Do not discontinue megestrol without first speaking to your doctor. In addition to its primary uses, megestrol is sometimes prescribed to treat malnutrition in cancer patients, prostate gland enlargement (prostatic hypertrophy), endometriosis (a condition where uterine-like tissue grows outside the uterus), and endometrial hyperplasia (an overgrowth of the uterine lining). Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for these conditions with your doctor. Before starting megestrol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to megestrol, any other medications, or any inactive ingredients in the tablets, suspension, or concentrated suspension. Request a list of inactive ingredients if needed. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take, especially antibiotics and indinavir (Crixivan). Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Notify your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, stroke, diabetes, or kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking megestrol, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication may harm the fetus. Do not breastfeed while on megestrol. Be aware that megestrol may disrupt the normal menstrual cycle in women, but this does not guarantee that pregnancy is impossible. Use reliable contraception to prevent pregnancy. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking megestrol. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking megestrol. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Megestrol may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if any of the following minor side effects persist or worsen: impotence, decreased sexual desire, unexpected vaginal bleeding, difficulty sleeping, gas, or rash. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. These include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, weakness, blurred vision, extreme thirst, frequent urination, extreme hunger, leg pain, difficulty breathing, sharp or crushing chest pain, slow or slurred speech, or weakness or numbness in an arm or leg. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Store megestrol in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments while taking megestrol. Your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to the medication. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Megestrol is sold under the brand names Megace® and Megace® ES.
